title: kv-cache-attn-seqlen-edgecase-debug-scratchpad-22
content:
Purpose: scratchpad for reproducing and debugging the KV-cache + attention-kernel selection edge-case that surfaces for certain sequence length distributions (observed in prod on some multi-turn chat workloads).

Summary of the issue (high level):
- Under high-turn dialogues (long total context via KV cache), some requests drop tokens / produce truncated outputs without an explicit OOM.
- Repro shows incorrect attention results when partial sequence-length mismatch occurs between the cached prefix and the current request. Suspect kernel selection + KV offset handling bug.

Where it was first seen:
- Customer logs from dedicated cluster us-west-2-dedicated-3 (support ticket #CS-2219).
- Reproduced locally on dev-gpu-rt-03 with Docker image: redwood/serving-runtime:canary-2024-10-18

Commands and reproductions tried: (notes + outputs)
1) Minimal repro script (python) -> reproduces mismatch reproducibly with model "rwkv-7b" variant and seqlen combos
- cmd: python reproduce_seqlen_bug.py --model rwkv-7b --cache-prefix 2048 --request-seqlen 512 --batch 1
- observed: final tokens missing 14-27 tokens consistently, no OOM, exit code 0

2) Kernel forcing experiments (env overrides):
- REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL=auto (default) => buggy behavior seen
- REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL=flash_attention => buggy (same symptoms)
- REDWOOD_ATTENTION_KERNEL=cutlass => behavior disappears (outputs match expected golden run)
- Note: forcing 'cutlass' increases latency ~1.4x but is a useful diagnostic

3) KV cache read checks (binary dump inspection):
- Ran dump_kv_cache_bin.py that serializes KV cache per layer after prefix build.
- For failing runs, layer 9..11 have expected shapes but some buffer offsets appear shifted by +128 (bytes) for cached keys (suspect pointer arithmetic in attention kernel path).
- Hex snippet (layer 10 keys start):
  good: 0x7f8c10a0  3f 9e 8b ...
  bad:  0x7f8c10a0  00 00 00 ... (zeroed region) then later non-zero at 0x7f8c1180

4) Bisection on seq len:
- prefix=1536 + request=256 -> OK
- prefix=1536 + request=512 -> fails
- prefix=1536 + request=768 -> fails
- prefix=1024 + request=512 -> flaky
- Hypothesis: something happens when total cached length crosses 2^n boundary (maybe tile-size alignment).

5) Single-layer isolation test:
- Modified runtime to run attention on single target layer (hook). Fail reproduces when layer > 8. Layers 0..7 OK. Suggests per-layer stride or layout change after some layers (maybe due to fp16 packing in larger matrices).

Observed error snippets / logs:
- No stacktrace in normal logs. I get these WARNs occasionally:
  WARN runtime::kernel_selector - selected kernel=flash_attention_fast for seqlen=512 total=2048 (estimated shared mem=48KB)
  WARN runtime::kv_cache - read_back returned 4096 != expected 4096 (shadow check ok)
- Downstream generation: truncated output (decoder stops generating mid-stream) but no exception.

Hypotheses so far: (ranked)
1) Kernel-specific path has a bug in computing KV buffer offsets when cached prefix length + request length crosses a tile or alignment boundary (most likely). cutlass path uses different indexing -> works.
2) Some layers switch to a different packing format after layer idx >= 8 (maybe because of vectorization/blocking heuristics), and the kernel selector doesn't adjust the offset formula accordingly.
3) Memory-copy race or incorrect memcpy size when copying cached keys from GPU <-> host (less likely given reproducibility on pinned-local runs).
4) A shape inference bug: the runtime's KV cache shape metadata doesn't update when we re-use a KV cache between requests with different request lengths, leading to reads from stale offsets.

Quick checks to test hypotheses:
- Force kernel=flash_attention but patch offset computation to use debug + instrumented asserts (added logs in kernel_selector.cpp). Reproduces (offset logs show +128 shift when failing).
- Mark layer packing disabled (force simple packing) -> repro disappears.
- Run with ASAN-enabled CPU build -> no relevant issues (this is GPU-only path).

Temporary mitigations (patches tried):
- Fallback policy adjusted: if total_context_length % tile_size == 0 then prefer cutlass kernel. Deployable as a stop-gap in Dedicated clusters (config flag).
- Added KV-cache consistency check after prefix load: compute CRC32 per layer and compare; when mismatch detected, rebuild cache and fall back to cutlass kernel.

Patch notes (local branches):
- git branch av/kv-offset-debug-2024-10-30 -> added verbose logs + runtime assert in kernel_selector
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/984 (WIP) includes tests and a small offset-calc fix (needs perf review)

Test matrix summary:
- Model variants: rwkv-7b, rwkv-15b (both affected), llama-2-13b (not affected in current quick tests)
- Batch sizes: 1 = deterministic; >1 increases failure rate (race amplification?)
- GPUs: A100 (driver 535) repros; RTX6000 did not repro locally (different kernel selection heuristics)

Next steps / TODOs: (ordered)
- [ ] Add unit tests that simulate packed vs simple key layouts and verify offset math.
- [ ] Add a synthetic kernel_selector unit test (C++ level) that checks offsets across layer indices and tile sizes.
- [ ] Expand dump_kv_cache to include per-layer packing metadata and CRC output for easier triage.
- [ ] If PR#984 passes basic CI, run performance benchmarks to measure cutlass vs flash_attention for seqlen distributions seen in prod.
- [ ] Coordinate with release-engineering to stage a canary with fallback rule for dedicated customers (low-risk config toggle).
- [ ] Loop in hw-optim team (Lucas) to sanity check kernel selection heuristics and packing thresholds.

Notes / breadcrumbs (mini-log):
- 2024-10-18: First reproed in CI by Maya on canary image
- 2024-10-21: Found kernel forcing abolishes issue (cutlass)
- 2024-10-24: Binary KV dump shows offset shifts in layers 9..12
- 2024-10-28: Created this scratchpad and added tracing in kernel_selector
- 2024-10-30: Opened WIP PR with fix-ish (av/kv-offset-debug-2024-10-30)

Questions for reviewers / running notes to self:
- Is there any recent change in packing heuristics or vectorization threshold that landed in July/Aug? (check changelog / commit history for commit message containing "packing" or "block_size")
- Should we add a runtime assert that verifies kv buffer live addresses align to expected tile boundaries after prefix load? Might be heavy in perf but OK behind debug flag.
- If we adopt fallback rule (prefer cutlass when total_context % tile_size == 0), what's the telemetry we should emit (metric name + tags) so we can easily roll back if perf impact is bad?

Links:
- Linear: https://linear.app/REDWOOD/issue/L-412-kv-cache-seqlen-edgecase
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/984
- Confluence draft: confluence://serving-runtime/kv-cache-seqlen-breadcrumbs

Scratchpad final note: keep this doc rough. If we get reproducible unit tests and the PR, produce a polished postmortem in shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/incidents/ with timeline + customer impact.
